topicName: SSH Connection Plugins and Multiplexing Optimization
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"SSH Connection Plugins and Multiplexing Optimization in Ansible"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"By default, Ansible uses the standard OpenSSH client to establish remote connections to managed nodes. While secure and reliable, the default behavior of opening a new SSH connection for every single task can create a massive performance bottleneck, especially when managing hundreds of servers."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding Ansible SSH Connection Plugins"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ansible delegates the connection task to connection plugins. The primary plugin used for Linux and UNIX targets is the 'ssh' plugin. Another alternative is the 'paramiko' plugin, which is a pure Python implementation of SSH, but it lacks advanced features like ControlPersist."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"What is SSH Multiplexing?"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"SSH multiplexing (ControlMaster and ControlPersist) allows multiple simultaneous SSH sessions to be routed through a single, established TCP socket connection. Instead of performing the cryptographic handshake and authentication phase repeatedly for every task in a playbook, Ansible pays the performance cost only once during the initial connection."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuring Multiplexing in ansible.cfg"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable and optimize SSH multiplexing, you need to modify your 'ansible.cfg' file. Below is a production-ready configuration block optimized for speed and reliability."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"[defaults]
inventory = inventory.ini
remote_user = ubuntu
host_key_checking = False

[ssh_connection]
ssh_args = -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=60s -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no
pipelining = True"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Breakdown of the Configuration Parameters"},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ControlMaster=auto: Tells the SSH client to attempt to reuse an existing master connection or create one if it does not exist."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ControlPersist=60s: Keeps the master connection open in the background for 60 seconds after the initial Ansible task finishes, allowing subsequent tasks to reuse it without re-authenticating."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"pipelining = True: Reduces the number of SSH operations required to execute a module on the remote server by executing modules via standard input without transferring separate script files."},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"Verifying Performance Improvements"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can measure the impact of enabling pipelining and multiplexing by running a simple playbook with the timer callback enabled. Notice how tasks that previously took several seconds per host now execute almost instantaneously."},{"order":16,"type":"code","text":"ANSIBLE_STDOUT_CALLBACK=timer ansible-playbook site.yml"}]
